 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:17.10.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.1381/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE II ADDITIONAL DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MACT.,HASSAN, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR DISMISSAL, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.1381/2015, dated 17.10.2017, on the file of II Additional District and Sessions Judge & NC: 2023:KHC:41251 Additional MACT., Hassan, whereby the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.1,12,800/- as compensation/granted meager amount of compensation.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge & NC: 2023:KHC:41251 Additional MACT., Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.6,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.

The case of the claimant is that, on 15.01.2015 at about 6.00 P.M., she was standing in front of the house, at that time, the driver of the Tata Indica Car came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the claimant, as a result of which, she sustained grievous injuries and spent huge amount for treatment.
As per the evidence of the Doctor and as per Ex.P5, there is pain and swelling of back bone over leg and X-ray shows fracture of both L2 vertebra.
According to the Doctor, she has sustained 25% disability to the whole body.
The Court below considering 25% to the limb and had taken 8% to the whole body.

According to the claimant,
she is an agriculturist and earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month and as no NC:
2023:KHC:41251 evidence is adduced in that regard.

The Court below had taken Rs.5,000/- as income and by applying the multiplier 16 and the disability at 8%, granted an amount of Rs.6,800/-
Sowbhagya vs The Manager on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52699565/
2 under the head of loss of future income; towards medical expenses 10,000/-; pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-; Conveyance charges Rs.500/-; Attendant charges Rs.500/- and in total compensation of amount of Rs.1,12,800/- was granted.
3.

Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that she has sustained the fracture of both L2 vertebra and granting of an amount of Rs.25,000/- under the head of pain and suffering is on the lower side.
He submits that no amount is granted either under the head of loss of amenities or under the head of loss of income during the laid up period.
It is further submitted that the income was taken at Rs.5,000/- which is on the lower side as the accident had taken place in the year 2015.
It is submitted that the compensation that is awarded by the Tribunal is not a reasonable compensation.
Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that, as the claimant has failed to prove the income, the Court below had rightly taken the income of the claimant at Rs.5,000/-.

It is submitted that the compensation that was granted on all the heads is just and reasonable compensation and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
5.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side.
Perused the entire material on record.
6. In this case the claimant has sustained pain and swelling of back bone over leg and fracture of both L2 vertebra.

Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant, under the head of pain and suffering, this Court is inclined to grant Rs.40,000/-; towards medical expenses Court had granted Rs.10,000/-; basing on the evidence and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the said finding.
Then coming to the conveyance, attendant and for extra nourishment granting an amount of Rs.15,000/-; is on the lower side.

Considering the injuries and the pain NC: 2023:KHC:41251 and swelling of back bone over leg and fracture of both L2 vertebra and when it comes to loss of future income considering the accident is of the year 2015, this Court is inclined to take Rs.9,000/- as a income.
The Court below had rightly considered the disability at 8% i.e., Rs.9,000x12x16x8/100 is Rs.1,38,240/-.
The Court below has failed to grant compensation under the head of loss of income during the laid up period as well as the amenities.

As this Court has already considered the income at 9000x2 is inclined to grant Rs.18,000/-, under the head loss of income during laid up period,
then towards loss of amenities, considering the injury to the back, this Court is inclined to grant Rs.
15,000/-.

7. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1 , the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
